detail.readme:
🤔🎞️ Video-of-Thought: Step-by-Step Video Reasoning
from Perception to Cognition

ICML 2024 (Oral)

Hao Fei, Shengqiong Wu, Wei Ji, Hanwang Zhang, Meishan Zhang, Mong Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

**Video-of-Thought (VoT)** brings chain-of-thought reasoning to video. It decomposes a complex video question into five sub-problems that move from **low-level pixel perception** (which objects matter, where they are, how they move) to **high-level cognition** (what the actions imply, which answer is most plausible, and whether that answer survives a perception- and commonsense-based check). The perception side is powered by **MotionEpic**, a video MLLM that reads and generates **spatial-temporal scene graphs (STSGs)** for fine-grained, pixel-level grounding. This repository is a complete, tested re-implementation of the paper: * 🧠 **The VoT reasoning engine**: all five steps with the paper's prompts, multiple-choice and open-ended QA, ranking, and verification with Step-4 re-execution. It works with any video LLM. * 🔌 **An API version that needs no training**: run VoT on GPT-4o/GPT-5, Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM/SGLang with Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL, ...), optionally grounded on STSGs from a detector + tracker or a VLM parser. * 🎞️ **MotionEpic**: the CLIP ViT-L/14 + Q-Former + recurrent graph transformer + Vicuna (LoRA) architecture, the five video–STSG grounding objectives, and the three-stage training recipe. * 📊 **Benchmarks**: converters and paper-style reports for NExT-QA, STAR, VLEP, IntentQA, Social-IQ, Causal-VidQA, MSR-VTT-QA and ActivityNet-QA, plus a resumable evaluation runner.

--- ## 📰 News * **2025-09** — Codebase updated with API version. * **2024-07** — VoT presented as an oral paper at ICML 2024. ## 📑 Contents [Method](#-method) · [Installation](#-installation) · [Quick start](#-quick-start) · [API version](#-the-api-version) · [MotionEpic](#%EF%B8%8F-motionepic-training) · [Evaluation](#-evaluation) · [Configuration](#%EF%B8%8F-configuration) · [Repository layout](#-repository-layout) · [Citation](#-citation) --- ## 🔍 Method ### Spatial-temporal scene graphs as the grounding interface A video is sampled into frames; each frame carries a scene graph whose nodes are objects `(label, feature, bbox)` and whose edges are `subject–predicate–object` triplets. **Temporal coreference edges** link the same object across adjacent frames, so a tracklet is simply a connected path through the STSG. MotionEpic reads STSGs through a graph encoder and *writes* them as text, which makes the grounding explicit, checkable and reusable by later reasoning steps.

```text Frame 1: { Objects: [{"car-1": [0.0, 13.4, 7.0, 8.1]}, {"street": [9.0, 13.5, 16.5, 15.0]}], Triplets: [("car-1", "on the left", "street")] } ... Temporal Coreference Edge: [ {Frame 1 -> 2: [("car-1", "car-1"), ("street", "street")]} ] ``` `vot.stsg` provides the data model, a serializer/parser for this grammar (tolerant to the formatting slips of real model outputs), tracklet extraction, k-hop neighbour scenes and target-to-node matching. ### MotionEpic

| Component | Paper setting | Code | |---|---|---| | LLM | Vicuna-7B v1.5, frozen + LoRA | `vot/models/motionepic/modeling.py` | | Video encoder | CLIP ViT-L/14, frozen, 8 fps | `vot/models/motionepic/vision.py` | | Projector | Q-Former | `vot/models/motionepic/projector.py` | | STSG encoder | Graph Transformer with recurrent propagation over frames (6 layers, 768-d), CLIP RoI features as node init | `vot/models/motionepic/stsg_encoder.py`, `featurizer.py` | | Grounding-aware tuning | L1 video–STSG matching, L2 video→STSG, L3 action→tracklets, L4 object→action + tracklets, L5 bbox→label + tracklet | `vot/data/grounding_tasks.py` | ### The five reasoning steps
| | Step | Produces | |---|---|---| | ① | **Task definition & target identification** — which objects does the question involve? | `[Target]` | | ② | **Object tracking** — output the partial STSG (tracklets) of the targets | `[Target Tracklet]` | | ③ | **Action analysing** — interpret the tracklets and their neighbour scenes with commonsense | `[Observation & Implication]` | | ④ | **QA via ranking** — score every candidate 1–10 with a rationale, then rank (open-ended questions first generate candidates) | `[Answer]` | | ⑤ | **Answer verification** — check the answer against the pixel grounding (perception) and the observations (cognition); on failure, record why and re-run ④ | verified answer | Every intermediate output is recycled as the input of the next step, and the full trace (prompts, responses, parsed values, token usage) is returned with the answer.
--- ## 📦 Installation ```bash git clone https://github.com/scofield7419/Video-of-Thought.git cd Video-of-Thought conda create -n vot python=3.10 -y && conda activate vot pip install -e ".[api,video]" # reasoning engine + API backends + video decoders # pip install -e ".[grounding]" # + Grounding DINO STSG provider # pip install -e ".[train]" # + MotionEpic training / local inference (PyTorch, transformers, peft, deepspeed) # pip install -e ".[all]" ``` The core package depends only on `numpy`, `Pillow`, `PyYAML` and `tqdm`; heavier dependencies are imported lazily by the components that need them. ## 🚀 Quick start **1. Offline walk-through (no model, no key).** A rule-based stand-in answers each step from an illustrative STSG, so you can inspect the exact prompts and the verification loop: ```bash python examples/offline_demo.py --trace python examples/offline_demo.py --reject-first # the first verification fails -> Step 4 is re-executed ``` **2. One question from the command line.** ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY=... # or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... vot run --video demo.mp4 \ --question "What is the relationship between the white truck and this neighborhood?" \ --options "Transportation" "Buildings" "Clean Services" "Entertainment Facilities" \ --backend openai:gpt-4o --out trace.json -v ``` **3. Python API.** ```python from vot import VideoOfThought, VoTConfig, build_backend model = build_backend("anthropic:claude-opus-5-5", cache=".cache/vot.sqlite") vot = VideoOfThought(model, VoTConfig(fps=1.0, max_frames=16)) res = vot("demo.mp4", "What is the relationship between the white truck and this neighborhood?", ["Transportation", "Buildings", "Clean Services", "Entertainment Facilities"]) print(res.pretty()) # answer, per-option scores, targets, tracklet size, verification res.partial_stsg # the grounded tracklets (an STSG object) res.trace # every prompt / response / parsed value ``` Open-ended questions: omit the options; VoT generates and ranks candidates (Step 4-Pre). ## 🔌 The API version VoT's reasoning chain is independent of how the model is trained. The API version keeps all five steps and realises the two non-text inputs for off-the-shelf models: the video becomes captioned frames (`Frame k (t=…s)`), and STSGs become their text expression plus a compact grammar specification. Because general-purpose models localise objects poorly, Step 2 can be anchored to an explicit STSG: | `step2_mode` | Grounding source | Behaviour | |---|---|---| | `generate` | none (STSG-free) | the model writes the targets' partial STSG from the frames, as MotionEpic does | | `select` | full STSG from a provider | the model picks the relevant tracklets; boxes are snapped to the reference | | `match` | full STSG from a provider | targets are matched to nodes programmatically, without an LLM call | ```bash # Grounding DINO + IoU tracking builds the STSG, the API model reasons over it vot run --video demo.mp4 --question "..." --options ... \ --backend openai:gpt-4o --stsg-provider detector --config configs/vot/api_grounded.yaml # open-source VLM behind an OpenAI-compatible server vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 32}' vot run ... --backend openai:Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct --base-url http://localhost:8000/v1 # inspect a parsed STSG vot stsg --video demo.mp4 --provider vlm --backend openai:gpt-4o --out demo_stsg.json --viz viz/ ``` Backends, providers, cost per instance and caching are described in [docs/api_version.md](docs/api_version.md). Any other model can be plugged in by implementing one method ([examples/custom_backend.py](examples/custom_backend.py)). ## 🎞️ MotionEpic training The full training stack is included for reproducibility. As in the paper, the video encoder and the LLM stay frozen; the Q-Former projector, the STSG encoder and LoRA adapters are trained. | Stage | Data | Objective | Trainable | |---|---|---|---| | 1. Video pre-training | WebVid captions | caption generation | projector | | 2. Grounding-aware tuning | Action Genome (10K manual STSGs) + 350K WebVid videos with parsed STSGs | L1–L5 | projector, STSG encoder, LoRA | | 3. Video instruction tuning | VideoChat + Video-ChatGPT instructions | instruction following | projector, STSG encoder, LoRA | | (4. Task fine-tuning) | benchmark training splits | QA | projector, STSG encoder, LoRA | ```bash python scripts/data/convert_action_genome.py --help # AG annotations -> STSG JSON python scripts/data/build_grounding_corpus.py --help # STSG JSON -> L1-L5 instruction data bash scripts/train/stage2_grounding.sh # see docs/training.md for all stages vot run --backend motionepic:checkpoints/motionepic-stage3 --config configs/vot/motionepic.yaml ... ``` Recipes, data formats and hyper-parameters: [docs/training.md](docs/training.md). **Model weights are not released**; the API version is the ready-to-use path. ## 📊 Evaluation ```bash # 1) convert the official annotations to the unified JSONL format python scripts/data/prepare_videoqa.py --benchmark nextqa --raw data/nextqa/raw/val.csv --split val \ --out data/nextqa/val.jsonl # 2) run a method (resumable; per-instance traces with --save-trace) vot eval --benchmark nextqa --data data/nextqa/val.jsonl --video-root data/nextqa/videos \ --backend openai:gpt-4o --config configs/vot/api.yaml --method vot \ --workers 8 --cache .cache/nextqa.sqlite --out results/nextqa/gpt4o_vot.jsonl # -> results/nextqa/gpt4o_vot.report.{json,md}: Acc@All / Acc@C / Acc@T / Acc@D, token usage ``` Supported benchmarks and their metrics are listed in [docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md). `--method cot` and `--method direct` run the paper's baselines with the same backend and frames. Results reported in the paper (MotionEpic, fine-tuned setting unless noted): | Benchmark | Metric | MotionEpic + CoT | **MotionEpic + VoT** | |---|---|:-:|:-:| | NExT-QA | Acc@All / C / T / D | 72.2 / 73.4 / 69.1 / 80.7 | **76.0 / 75.8 / 74.6 / 83.3** | | STAR | Int. / Seq. / Pre. / Fea. | 66.8 / 69.6 / 60.6 / 57.4 | **71.5 / 72.6 / 66.6 / 62.7** | | VLEP | Acc | 68.2 | **73.4** | | IntentQA | Acc | 66.1 | **70.8** | | Social-IQ | 2-way / 4-way | 71.7 / 43.0 | **72.8 / 45.0** | | Causal-VidQA | D / E / P-AR / C-AR | 78.5 / 77.2 / 52.4 / 55.0 | **81.2 / 83.0 / 54.7 / 58.6** | | Zero-shot | MSR-VTT / ActivityNet / NExT-QA / STAR | 63.1 / 50.0 / 61.9 / 56.5 | **66.2 / 54.6 / 66.5 / 61.7** |

## ⚙️ Configuration `VoTConfig` (YAML presets in [`configs/vot/`](configs/vot)) exposes the design choices of each step: | Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `fps`, `max_frames` | 1.0, 16 | frame sampling (MotionEpic preset: 8 fps, 32 frames) | | `context` | `chain` | Steps 1–3 share one dialogue, or every step is an `isolated` slot-filled call | | `step2_mode` | `auto` | `generate` / `select` / `match` (see the API version) | | `neighbor_hops` | 1 | neighbour scenes added around the tracklets for Step 3 | | `ranking` | `model` | `model` (Step 4-B prompt), `auto` (only on ties), `score` (no ranking call) | | `num_open_candidates` | 4 | candidates generated for open-ended questions | | `multi_answer` | false | "choose all possible correct option(s)" task definition | | `verify_perception`, `verify_cognition` | true, true | the two verification perspectives (Table 4 ablations) | | `max_verify_rounds` | 2 | re-executions of Step 4 after a failed verification | Override any field on the command line with `--set key=value`, e.g. `--set ranking=auto --set max_frames=8`. ## 🗂 Repository layout ```text vot/ ├── stsg/ STSG data model, expression grammar (format/parse), matching, graph ops ├── video/ frame sampling (decord / PyAV / OpenCV / frame folders), visualisation ├── reasoning/ VoT engine (vot.py), paper prompts, parsers, results/traces, CoT & direct baselines ├── backends/ VideoLLM interface; OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, MotionEpic, mock; response cache ├── grounding/ STSG providers: static annotations, VLM parser, detector + tracker ├── models/motionepic/ vision tower, Q-Former, recurrent graph transformer, featurizer, MLLM ├── data/ unified VideoQA format, benchmark converters, L1–L5 grounding tasks, SFT datasets ├── train/ MotionEpic training (HF Trainer, DeepSpeed) ├── eval/ metrics and paper-style reports, benchmark runner └── cli.py `vot run | eval | stsg` configs/ VoT presets, training stages, DeepSpeed scripts/ data preparation and training launchers examples/ offline demo, API quick start, custom backend docs/ method-to-code map, API version, training, benchmarks tests/ unit and end-to-end tests (offline) ``` Run the test suite with `pytest -q` (no GPU, network or API key needed). ## 📖 Documentation * [docs/method.md](docs/method.md) — paper-to-code map and implementation decisions * [docs/api_version.md](docs/api_version.md) — backends, STSG providers, cost, zero-shot protocol * [docs/training.md](docs/training.md) — MotionEpic data preparation and training stages * [docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md) — datasets, conversion and metrics ## 📝 Citation ```bibtex @inproceedings{fei2024video, title = {Video-of-Thought: Step-by-Step Video Reasoning from Perception to Cognition}, author = {Fei, Hao and Wu, Shengqiong and Ji, Wei and Zhang, Hanwang and Zhang, Meishan and Lee, Mong-Li and Hsu, Wynne}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning}, series = {Proceedings of Machine Learning Research}, volume = {235}, pages = {13109--13125}, year = {2024} } ``` ## 🙏 Acknowledgements MotionEpic builds on [Vicuna](https://huggingface.co/lmsys/vicuna-7b-v1.5), [CLIP](https://huggingface.co/openai/clip-vit-large-patch14), [BLIP-2](https://huggingface.co/Salesforce/blip2-opt-2.7b) and the [Graph Transformer](https://github.com/graphdeeplearning/graphtransformer);
